summary_hint: Service invoice from <vendor_name> for <service_description>: <total_amount> (loan <loan_number>). A bill, not a receipt.

typed_core.name: vendor_name
typed_core.why: identity — the service provider billing (loan processor, surveyor, credit/title vendor, etc.)
typed_core.prompt_hint: The vendor/issuer name on the invoice

typed_core.name: invoice_number
typed_core.why: identity — the vendor's invoice id, when printed
typed_core.prompt_hint: Only if an 'INVOICE #' is printed (some invoices have none)

typed_core.name: due_date
typed_core.why: processor — the payment due date, when printed
typed_core.prompt_hint: Only if printed; leave null otherwise

typed_core.name: bill_to_name
typed_core.why: identity — who the invoice is billed to (may be the borrower, the lender, or a broker)

typed_core.name: loan_number
typed_core.why: identity — the loan the invoice relates to, when printed (ties the invoice to the file)
typed_core.prompt_hint: Only if a loan number is printed; captured verbatim, masked at the snapshot boundary by the global PII registry

typed_core.name: borrower_name
typed_core.why: identity — the borrower, when named (often coincides with bill_to_name, but a lender-billed invoice may differ)
typed_core.prompt_hint: Only if a borrower is named distinctly

typed_core.name: property_address
typed_core.why: identity — the property the service was for, when printed
typed_core.prompt_hint: e.g. a 'FOR:' line or property reference; leave null if absent

typed_core.name: service_description
typed_core.why: processor — what was billed (e.g. 'Third Party Loan Processing', 'Survey Fee', 'Credit Report')
typed_core.prompt_hint: The service/line description; if several lines, the primary/summary description

typed_core.name: total_amount
typed_core.why: processor — the invoice total (the amount owed)

rejected.name: line_items[]
rejected.reason: both sampled invoices are SINGLE-LINE (064 one description + total; 058's table is one 'Survey Fee' line + 10 EMPTY template rows). A single service_description + total_amount suffices; an unused list is plumbing for nothing (A4). Add it only when a genuine multi-line invoice appears.

rejected.name: amount_paid / payment_status / balance_due
rejected.reason: an invoice is a BILL (what is OWED), not a receipt. The paid/receipt side is the existing appraisal_payment / evidence_of_payment types. Neither is printed on the samples; adding them would blur the invoice/receipt line.

rejected.name: loan_originator_name / processor_name / vendor_nmls
rejected.reason: processing-invoice-specific fields (on 064) — this is ONE generic vendor-invoice type; vendor-specific fields do not generalise (four of six samples are one processor = one borrower's workflow, not a market pattern). Catch-all.

rejected.name: is_valid / is_reasonable / fee_is_customary
rejected.reason: JUDGMENTS, not facts. Tags describe; rules judge.

encoding_variations: one GENERIC type across vendor kinds — processing (HR Loan Processing), survey (Van Metre), credit-order, title, etc.
fields are INCONSISTENT across vendor kinds: 064 has a loan number but no invoice number; 058 has an invoice number and a property ('FOR:') but no loan number — hence most fields optional
bill_to_name often equals the borrower; a lender-billed invoice may name the lender (e.g. 'UWM') separately
single-line is the norm; a 'DESCRIPTION/AMOUNT' table may be a template with empty rows

open_questions.q: Separate types per vendor kind (processing / survey / credit)?
open_questions.recommendation: ONE generic type (GEET'S DECISION, LP-467): four of six samples are one processor (HR Loan Processing) — that is one borrower's workflow, not a market pattern; a processing_invoice type would not generalise.

notes: Serves NO rule (rules_served empty) — low value per document (vendor, amount, loan number), but six documents and a trivial schema; earns a catalog entry on processor visibility (ADR-362/363), keeping them out of `unknown`.

loan_number reuses the existing global _PII_FIELDS 'loan_number' registration (masked). invoice_number is left UNMASKED (a vendor invoice id a processor needs to read; short on samples) — a rare 9+-digit bare invoice number is an accepted residual.
service_description gets the 9+-digit scrub backstop (_SCRUB_FREE_TEXT_FIELDS) in case a description embeds a bare loan number.
